history.heading: Carthage
paragraphs: Tunisia, on the North African coast, was home to Amazigh (Berber) peoples. Phoenicians from Tyre founded Carthage, near present-day Tunis, traditionally in 814 BCE. Carthage became a great maritime power that fought Rome in the Punic Wars; Hannibal crossed the Alps with elephants. Rome destroyed Carthage in 146 BCE and later rebuilt it as the capital of the province of Africa, famous for its grain and mosaics, as seen at El Jem's amphitheatre.

history.heading: Islamic Tunisia
paragraphs: Arab armies brought Islam in the 7th century and founded Kairouan, one of Islam's holy cities. The Aghlabids, Fatimids and Hafsids ruled from Tunisia, and Tunis became a great city. The Ottomans took control in the 16th century, and Tunisia was governed by semi-autonomous beys. In 1846 Tunisia became one of the first Muslim countries to abolish slavery.

history.heading: French protectorate and independence
paragraphs: France made Tunisia a protectorate in 1881. Habib Bourguiba led the independence movement, and Tunisia became independent on 20 March 1956. As president, Bourguiba modernised the country and granted women extensive rights through the Personal Status Code. Zine El Abidine Ben Ali took power in 1987 and ruled in an authoritarian way.

In December 2010, the self-immolation of street vendor Mohamed Bouazizi sparked the Tunisian Revolution, which ousted Ben Ali in January 2011 and launched the Arab Spring. Tunisia adopted a democratic constitution in 2014, and its National Dialogue Quartet won the 2015 Nobel Peace Prize. In 2021 President Kais Saied suspended parliament and later rewrote the constitution, concentrating power.

culture.heading: Mediterranean culture
paragraphs: Arabic is the official language, Tunisian Arabic (Derja) is spoken daily, and French is widely used. Most Tunisians are Sunni Muslim, and Djerba has an ancient Jewish community. Tunisia has many UNESCO sites, including the medinas of Tunis and Sousse, Carthage and Kairouan.

Couscous, brik (a fried pastry), harissa and lablabi are favourites. The film Star Wars was partly filmed in Tunisia's desert towns. Football and handball are popular, and tennis player Ons Jabeur is a national icon.

politics.heading: Presidential system
paragraphs: Under the 2022 constitution, Tunisia has a strong presidential system with a weakened parliament. President Saied was re-elected in 2024 in a vote with low turnout, after many rivals were barred or jailed. Opposition figures, journalists and critics have been prosecuted. Tunisia is a major departure point for migrants trying to reach Europe.

economy.heading: Economic structure
paragraphs: Tunisia has a diversified economy with manufacturing (textiles, car parts and electronics, mostly for Europe), phosphates, olive oil (it is one of the world's largest exporters), tourism and services. The EU is its main trading partner.
High unemployment, especially among graduates, regional inequality, inflation and public debt are major challenges. Tunisia has rejected IMF loan conditions. The currency is the Tunisian dinar.
